alex: Heads up - ran a bring-up eval for the new reranker on biz-qa and saw NDCG drop ~0.06 for int8 vs fp32. Same weights, different build. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

maya: did you run the same eval harness + seed? which dataset split?

alex: yes, eval harness same, seed=42, holdout=dev-2026. Command:
```
python eval.py --model models/ranker/v2 --quant int8 --dataset biz-qa --split dev --seed 42 --topk 10
```

devon: can you paste the topk selection code? NDCG is sensitive to tie-handling when scores are equal-ish after quantization.

alex: here's the snippet from our eval util:
```
# pick topk
cands = sorted(cands, key=lambda x: x['score'], reverse=True)
return cands[:topk]
```

sasha: hmm sorted is stable in Python but if scores are floats very close, ordering depends on insertion order. Are you shuffling candidates anywhere earlier? That could flip ties differently for int8 vs fp32.

alex: we DO randomize candidate order during preprocessing to avoid label leakage. but we seed the RNG before eval. seed is same but quantization can change relative ordering due to rounding.

devon: two possible fixes: 1) apply a secondary deterministic tie-breaker (e.g., candidate id) in sort key, or 2) switch to `heapq.nlargest` with a deterministic comparator. try 1 first.

maya: agreed - also check that metric code uses strict > vs >= when computing rank. I once had an MRR bug where ties counted as hits at different ranks depending on comparator.

alex: good call. metric line is:
```
rank = next((i for i,c in enumerate(ranked) if c['label']==1), None)
```
so it returns first match which depends on ordering.

sasha: add `key=lambda x: (x['score'], x['cid'])` and ensure `cid` is stable string. that'll remove nondeterminism from score ties.

alex: trying now - re-running int8 eval with tie-breaker by cid.

ci-bot: build 2026.1759994280 started for eval-job alex/rerank-int8-repro

alex: re-run done. int8 NDCG delta reduced from 0.058 -> 0.005. MRR gap also nearly gone.

maya: nice. still worth auditing dataset for candidate duplicates - if two identical docs with different ids exist, tie-breaker will hide that.

devon: also log how many ties you had (abs(score_fp32 - score_int8) < 1e-6). could be an indicator.

alex: will add a small tie-report and update eval harness with stable sorting. thanks all :thumbsup:

sasha: can you open a tiny PR with the deterministic sort + a unit test that constructs equal-score items? should be quick.

alex: filing PR now: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rerank-harness/pulls/342

ci-bot: PR 342 opened by alex - tests running.

maya: great teamwork. keeping metric definitions deterministic saved us from chasing quant noise.

alex: leaving a short note in the onboarding doc about "stable top-k" so future bring-ups remember this.
